flows.description: Exercise owned temporary checkout cleanup on success, failure, cancellation and explicit debug retention, excluding environment and untracked inputs.

runtime.launch: Python unittest creates synthetic repositories and runner children in temporary directories.
runtime.health: Tests wait for actual child exit and inspect the ownership marker and retained directory.
runtime.cleanup: The runner terminates its process group; unittest TemporaryDirectory removes each owned fixture, including retained debug cases.

flows.description: Apply the complete D1 migration chain, seed the checked-in default synthetic scenario and assert local database invariants.

runtime.launch: The native db-reset and db-check commands run Wrangler against the isolated local synthetic D1 state.
runtime.health: Wrangler must finish migrations and the scenario invariant queries successfully.
runtime.cleanup: Each Wrangler process exits. The existing ignored worktree-local synthetic D1 database remains available for local development.

flows.description: Run Keel make verify: unchanged real PDF isolation probes, public-data scan, formatting, lint, types, all native unit/API/D1 tests, production builds and the complete desktop/mobile browser suite.

runtime.launch: Native PDF probes own rootless sandbox containers. Vitest fixtures own synthetic SQLite/workerd resources. make e2e resets its isolated D1 store and Playwright launches pnpm dev on worktree-specific ports.
runtime.health: Real PDF adversarial assertions, database readiness and Playwright webServer /api/alpha readiness must succeed before their dependent checks.
runtime.cleanup: PDF and Vitest fixtures dispose owned containers, workers and temporary files. Playwright stops its owned web/API process group; screenshots and traces stay in ignored native report directories. make e2e refuses server reuse through KEEL_E2E_ISOLATED=1.

requirements.description: Public repository inputs and fixtures remain synthetic; reject prohibited source-document formats and secret patterns. Semantic privacy and full-history secret review remain separately required.
D1 owns accepted application state; recorded evidence decisions, forecast snapshots and financial review history retain their accepted append-only and versioned boundaries.
Currency uses integer minor units and probabilities use integer ppm; missing financial facts stay unknown.
Zod validates external payloads and production authorization fails closed, including immediate credential revocation and private document access.

Routine source updates use recorded deterministic policies; identity, unsupported evidence, manual decisions and planning exceptions retain the accepted review boundaries. Duplicate and racing attempts converge.
User-facing reads serve D1 projections without reconciliation, provider/object reads, writes or per-row repository fanout.

Use existing 120-item or documented-maximum holdouts, fixed round-trip ceilings, full query ordering/history and unrelated households; inspect query plans and real index-inclusive D1 billing counters.
Preserve the accepted aggregate idle, failure and useful-work envelopes, freshness, atomic admission, retry/deadline/cancellation bounds and runtime inventory.
Shared components, minimal valid submissions, recorded routine updates, exceptional review, save/readback/retry behavior and desktop/mobile visual regressions follow Keel UI policy.
Keep the initial route shell and the existing 100 KiB gzip initial JavaScript ceiling enforced by the production build.
Real rootless PDF isolation and scanner probes remain mandatory, with existing resource limits, privacy, original-byte ownership and fail-closed evidence access.
Preserve bounded document backup/recovery and owned temporary artifact cleanup, active leases, cancellation and explicit seven-day debug retention; do not delete foreign artifacts.

Keep native gates, required test discovery, accepted source pins, exact-SHA deployment prerequisites, isolated unprivileged runner lanes, no remote seeding and existing backup/order/smoke safeguards. Hosted enforcement and live release evidence are separate.
